And the gorge river drops a MANDATORY swim into the middle of the jumping, with a rock rib to dive under and slot walls set twice-the-jump back from the landing so no bank bypasses it. The difficulty curve is thereby stated in geometry.

The shared haze is retuned from dense teal to thin grey-green air, because every scene in this game is above water and the underwater feel belongs to the water volumes, which tint it themselves; at the old density anything past thirty metres flattened into one plane and the valley rendered as an empty sea.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared triplanar world-space terrain shader exists with a small set of client-owned material resources, and Coral Cove's platforms, walls, beds and banks wear them rather than per-node flat colours — with the two mod gates keeping flat colour as the deliberate exception
The forest kit's five props are generated headless in Blender, deterministic under a seed, carry provenance records, and pass the Asset Contract validator inside the environment budget

A missed jump anywhere over the act-1 river costs a swim and never a life, while a fall in the glow grotto still costs a life at the last checkpoint: the pit volume sits between the route and the scenery forest floor and the waterway spans exactly the forgiving stretch

The gorge river is a mandatory swim between jump sections — entered from the landing, dived under the rib, exited onto the first terrace — and its slot walls stand at least twice the measured jump from any standable edge so the swim cannot be bypassed on a bank
Every water volume in the world carries bubble particles (the REQ-034 dressing rule), emitted by the same construction that makes the volume so a new river cannot ship without them
The retuned haze keeps distant geometry legible: rendered captures show the forest floor, trees and valley sides reading at route distance in every act, and the full verification chain stays green

requirements.name: Hero surface quality: baked character maps at toy-grade finish
requirements.description:
The hero must read as a finished toy at gameplay distance AND in a close-up: the reference is a well-made vinyl figure under studio light — pristine gloss, soft translucent skin, deep wet eyes — not a vertex-tinted mesh. This extends REQ-035 (Hero Character Look), whose final criterion (the maintainer sign-off render) has stayed unmet precisely because flat vertex colour under real lighting still reads as unfinished.

THE CHARACTER IS THE ONE ASSET THAT EARNS TEXTURES. The Asset Contract's surface doctrine says baked maps are the last resort, paid for only where a pattern must be AUTHORED rather than DESCRIBED — and the hero's skin is that case: mottling that follows anatomy, a belly-to-back gradient, pore-scale relief. So the Blender lane gains a bake stage: UV-unwrap the generated hero headless, bake fine-detail maps (albedo detail and normal) from procedural node trees in Cycles, and ship them beside the glb under the character category's documented size bounds, with the bake recorded in provenance like every other generation step.

THE ROLE MATERIALS finish the job in Godot, because most of the Astro Bot read is MATERIAL rather than map: subsurface scattering and a clearcoat sheen on skin so light enters rather than bounces; a high-gloss dark eye whose highlight is geometry (the gleam) and therefore never lost to environment reflections; gill fronds lit from behind through backlight so they glow when the sun crosses them; the baked normal map giving the skin its fine relief only at close range.

PERFORMANCE IS A CONSTRAINT, NOT A HOPE: the hero stays inside its existing Asset Contract triangle budget (the bake adds maps, never geometry), texture memory stays within the category's size bounds, and the whole dressed Coral Cove scene is measured — total triangles counted headlessly and the perf gate extended to run the valley — so desktop testing meets a scene in the tens of thousands of triangles, not hundreds.
acceptanceCriteria: The Blender lane bakes hero maps headless and reproducibly: the generated axolotl is UV-unwrapped and fine-detail albedo and normal maps are baked from procedural sources in one CLI invocation, recorded in the asset's provenance
Baked maps conform to the Asset Contract character category: PNG, within the documented size bounds, living in the asset's own directory, and the validator passes
The bake adds no geometry: the shipped hero's triangle count is unchanged and remains inside its Asset Contract budget

The skin role material carries the baked normal and detail maps with subsurface scattering and a clearcoat sheen; the eye is high-gloss with its highlight guaranteed by the gleam geometry; gills glow when backlit — all applied by the existing role classification at runtime

Rendered close-up and gameplay-distance captures on the shared rig show the finish: visible skin relief in close-up that vanishes into a clean silhouette at distance, no shading seam at any UV boundary
The dressed Coral Cove scene's total triangle count is measured headlessly and stays under 150,000, and the performance gate runs the valley world within the documented budgets

requirements.name: Hero anatomy fidelity: the maintainer's reference sheet, built
requirements.description:
The hero must match the maintainer's own reference sheet, reference/hero/01_hero_perspective.png, at professional game-character craft. This is the mesh half of the hero's look; REQ-033 owns its materials and REQ-040 its baked surface maps, and both were already met while the animal underneath still read as amateur.

THE TARGET CHANGED ONCE, ON THE MAINTAINER'S CALL, AND THE HISTORY MATTERS. This requirement was first written against "flush, detailed limbs, face doesn't look cartoonish, and the gills flow and look real", and built a realistic salamander: tiny lidless dorso-lateral eyes, a flat skull wedge, filaments massed radially around every gill stalk. The maintainer then supplied the reference sheet — which has LARGE round glossy eyes, a soft domed skull and a gentle smile — and chose it explicitly, knowing it pulls against "not cartoonish". Two criteria here were rewritten for that decision rather than the mesh being bent to keep them, and one threshold was lowered; each says so in its own text, because a criterion quietly relaxed to match what was built proves nothing.

WHAT THE REFERENCE ASKED FOR, AND WHAT WAS BUILT TO IT:
  * GILLS ARE FEATHERS ON LONG BARE STALKS. Each ramus is a stalk whose outer half only carries filaments, in ONE plane — a feather. The plume's volume comes from the three stalks pointing three ways (forward-up, out-up, back-up), not from massing filaments around each stalk. The bare inner half is what holds the fronds clear of the head instead of packing them against the neck.
  * THE TAIL FIN IS TRANSLUCENT. The dorsal and ventral membranes moved out of the skin role and into the gill role, because the gill material already does what the reference's tail does — subsurface scattering with a backlight through it. Their colours stay inside the gill range so the role's combined mean green keeps clearing GILL_MAX_GREEN with margin (0.428 against a 0.5 bound; an earlier paler fin left only 0.011).
  * THE FACE IS THE REFERENCE'S. Large glossy eyes with a geometry catchlight, a domed skull, a mouth seam placed against the skull's OWN cross-section — authored at a flat height it sank inside the head as soon as the head was domed, and a buried mouth renders as no mouth at all.

WHAT SURVIVED FROM THE REALISTIC PASS, because it was never in tension with the reference: limbs and toes grown as branches of one edge skeleton rather than joined afterwards (bpy.ops.object.join() merges mesh data and neither welds nor blends, so every limb had been a separate shell pushed into the body), four toes in front and five behind, a laterally compressed tail blade, and a dorsal crest that swells over the tail rather than running flat along the spine.

WHAT IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN HOPED. Silhouette quality resists testing, which is exactly why it drifts; these criteria pick the measurable consequences of the anatomy being right and measure them over the SHIPPED glb, so a regenerated hero fails with a number rather than in a screenshot nobody takes. The two sharpest were checked against the superseded mesh before being trusted: plume planarity separates one flat sheet (0.147) from three fanned feathers (0.273), and foot-to-body continuity separates 0 of 4 from 4 of 4.
acceptanceCriteria: The gill plumes have volume rather than lying in a plane: measured over one side's plume in the shipped model, the smallest principal spread of the filament mass is at least 0.22 of the largest. THE BAR MOVED WITH THE DESIGN: it was 0.30 against a build that massed filaments radially around every stalk and scored 0.512; the reference sheet's three flat feathers are inherently less voluminous and score 0.273, so the bar now sits between the two readings it must tell apart — 0.147 for one flat sheet, 0.273 for three fanned feathers
The skull is the widest part of the animal: the shipped mesh's maximum half-width forward of the shoulders exceeds its maximum half-width through the trunk behind them

The cross-section ratio inverts along the animal: the tail is laterally compressed (width below height) while the skull is wider than tall by at least 1.20. NOT the 1.5 a real salamander's flat wedge gives — the reference sheet's head is a soft dome and measures 1.39 — and the tail half still carries most of the discrimination at 0.62 against a bound of 1.0

The eye is the reference sheet's large glossy one rather than the small lidless amphibian eye an earlier build shipped: its radius is between a fifth and two fifths of the skull's half-width, and it sits off the centreline as one of a readable pair. THIS CRITERION WAS REWRITTEN, not relaxed — the maintainer chose the reference's eye over the realistic one, so the old "under a sixth" bound was describing a design that is no longer wanted
The generator builds limbs and toes as branches of one edge skeleton per role rather than as separate objects joined afterwards, so the shipped skin is continuous flesh at every limb join
The maintainer accepts rendered portraits of the shipped hero as matching their reference sheet at professional game-character craft
